candidates.exact_span: Placement of sewage sludge shall not contaminate an aquifer. This shall be demonstrated through one of the following:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether compliance must be shown by a groundwater monitoring program versus a scientist certification changes which monitoring obligations apply and what evidence type suffices when no ordinary numeric discharge result is available.

candidates.exact_span: Results of a ground-water monitoring program developed by a qualified ground-water scientist.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether this alternative imposes an ongoing groundwater monitoring requirement (and its scope) affects which monitoring obligations are applicable.

candidates.exact_span: A certification by a qualified ground-water scientist may be used to demonstrate that sewage sludge placed on an active sewage sludge unit does not contaminate an aquifer.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If certification is accepted instead of monitoring, required monitoring may be deemed not applicable; conversely, rejecting certification as sufficient leaves monitoring required or evidence unresolved for no-result periods.

candidates.exact_span: the concentration of methane gas in air in any structure within the surface disposal site shall not exceed 25% of the lower explosive limit for methane gas during the period that the sewage sludge unit is active.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This sets an enforceable numeric compliance threshold (25% of LEL); different readings of LEL basis, averaging period, or active-unit timing change whether reported methane measurements exceed the applicable limit.

candidates.exact_span: The concentration of methane gas in air at the property line of the surface disposal site shall not exceed the lower explosive limit for methane gas during the period that the sewage sludge unit is active.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This establishes a separate numeric limit at the property line (100% of LEL); interpretation of measurement location, LEL value, and active-period scope affects limit applicability and exceedance determinations.

Whether continuous methane monitoring is required—and what sampling frequency or gaps count as noncompliance—affects monitoring-obligation applicability and how missing or intermittent data are classified.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall be tested once during the life of the permit within one year from the effective date of the permit in accordance with the method specified at 40 CFR 268, Appendix I (Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP)) or other approved methods.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The once-per-permit-life timing window and method choice determine whether TCLP testing was required during Federal FY2025 and whether alternative approved methods satisfy the obligation.

candidates.exact_span: Sludge shall be tested after final treatment prior to leaving the POTW site.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of 'final treatment' and 'leaving the POTW site' affects when the TCLP test must occur and whether monitoring was required for sludge handled in FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge determined to be a hazardous waste in accordance with 40 CFR Part 261, shall be handled according to RCRA standards for the disposal of hazardous waste in accordance with 40 CFR Part262.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Hazardous-waste classification shifts which enforceable numeric limits and disposal-related monitoring/compliance frameworks apply instead of ordinary sludge surface-disposal limits.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall be tested at the frequency show below in Element 2, Section I.D. for PCBs.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Applicability and frequency of PCB testing depend on the cross-referenced Element 2, Section I.D.; different readings of that external frequency table change which FY2025 monitoring periods require PCB testing.

candidates.exact_span: Any sludge exceeding a concentration of 50 mg/Kg shall not be surface disposed.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This is an enforceable numeric PCB concentration limit; interpretation of units, sample basis, and comparison methodology affects whether reported PCB results exceed the applicable limit.

candidates.exact_span: All sewage sludge that is disposed of in a surface disposal site shall be treated by either the Class A or Class B pathogen requirements unless sewage sludge is placed on an active surface disposal site, and is covered with soil or other material at the end of each operating day.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The Class A/B treatment obligation versus daily-cover exception determines whether pathogen-related monitoring/treatment was required and how no-data or cover-only operations are categorized.

candidates.exact_span: When reporting on the DMR, list pathogen reduction level attained as A, B, or C (daily cover).
candidates.computation_change_reason: How DMR entries (or their absence) map to documented pathogen level A, B, or daily-cover category affects classification of missing-evidence cases versus established no-requirement or documented compliance states.

candidates.exact_span: When reporting how compliance was met, list Alternative 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6 for Class A, or Alternative Number 1, 2, 3, or 4 for Class B, on DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which alternative pathway was used (or left unreported) affects which underlying monitoring/testing obligations attach and whether missing DMR detail leaves applicability unresolved.

candidates.exact_span: All 6 alternatives require either the density of fecal coliform in the sewage sludge be less than 1000 MPN per gram of total solids (dry weight basis), or the density of Salmonella sp.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The fecal-coliform numeric threshold is an enforceable limit for Class A demonstrations; the truncated Salmonella criterion is incomplete in this segment, leaving ambiguity in which numeric limit applies and whether evidence is adequate when only partial criteria are visible.
